sources.title: Nonuniform Lower Bounds for Exponential Time Classes
sources.locator: Author draft dated February 16, 1995: Theorems 2.1–2.2, Corollaries 2.1–2.5, Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.1; printed pp.4–9
sources.read_depth: Recovered complete author PostScript, converted locally and read theorem statements with surrounding proof/quantifier context; publisher metadata checked.
sources.version_limitation: Author draft, with unfinished introductory wording; do not assert line-for-line identity with the MFCS 1995 published version. Publisher record supplies original publication year, not later digitization date.
sources.assessment: The advice exponents and circuit sizes are fixed constants. Relativized corollaries retain EXP with a stronger oracle. Neither EXP⊄Ppoly nor NEXP⊄NPpoly follows by taking a union over bounds.

sources.title: Separating Classes in the Exponential Time Hierarchy from Classes in PH
sources.locator: Author manuscript Corollary 3.1 p.9; Theorem 3.4 and Corollary 3.3 p.11; concluding discussion pp.11–12
sources.read_depth: Recovered full author PostScript; read Sections 3–4 and reference chain to Fu–Li–Zhong 1994.
sources.version_limitation: Author publications page uses the alternate manuscript title Using Bounded Query Classes to Separate Classes in the Exponential Time Hierarchy from Classes in PH; journal is TCS 158:221–231.
sources.assessment: Parallel NP queries and each fixed polynomial query bound are separated from NEXP. Unrestricted polynomially many adaptive NP queries remain a different target. Higher-level corollaries retain corresponding exponential-hierarchy levels. The already imported Theta2P noninclusion is corroborated; no Delta2P noninclusion is licensed.

sources.title: A Note on the Relationship of BPP and RP to Exponential Time Classes
sources.locator: Portland State TR02-1; Theorem 3.1; Corollaries 3.3–3.5 printed pp.3–4; discussion and Corollaries 3.7–3.8 p.5
sources.read_depth: Recovered full author PostScript and read all result statements, assumptions and adjacent proofs.
sources.assessment: BPP differs from ZPEXP with an RP oracle. P=RP implies BPP≠EXP; P=ZPP implies RP≠EXP. Oracle removal and circuit corollaries retain hypotheses. ZPEXP and its relativization are not roster synonyms for EXP.
sources.delta: No unconditional roster label. P=RP conditional EXP-versus-BPP statement already follows from baseline implications by contradiction.

sources.title: Unconditional Lower Bounds Against Advice
sources.read_depth: Read all result statements, their fixed-bound quantifiers, and the proof disjunction in Theorem 3; followed older references beyond the prior Theorem 6 check.
sources.assessment: Theorem 3 is NEXP⊄NP/n^c for each fixed c; its proof disjunction does not independently establish NEXP⊄NPpoly. Theorems 6 and 9 retain fixed query/time exponents. BPEXP and MAEXP remain distinct larger left classes in Theorems 13 and 15. Oracle equalities in Theorems 17–18 are neither ordinary containments nor ZFC independence. Theorem 22 uses coNEXP advice, not coNP.

sources.title: Hierarchies for Semantic Classes
sources.locator: STOC 2005 extended abstract; Theorems 1–3 and Section 4.2; printed p.2 onward
sources.read_depth: Read formal theorem statements and advice conventions, beyond the earlier bibliography reference.
sources.assessment: The semantic hierarchies retain advice in the harder class, including one-bit advice cases. They cannot be read as uniform BPP or ZPP hierarchies separating roster EXP/NEXP comparisons.

sources.title: A Generic Time Hierarchy With One Bit of Advice
sources.locator: Theorems 1–4, printed pp.3–4; introduction on uniform semantic hierarchies
sources.read_depth: Read the 2006 primary version theorem statements and advice quantifiers; checked 2007 journal metadata, not its entire proof text.
sources.assessment: The harder machines retain advice. Removing one advice bit is not an innocuous conversion to an ordinary uniform class. Positive advice is especially material for semantic classes.

sources.title: New Non-uniform Lower Bounds for Uniform Classes
sources.locator: Theorems 1.1–1.4, author manuscript pp.1–2; Section 7 extension scope
sources.read_depth: Read complete introductory theorem statements and definitions of advice, NP-uniform circuits and RE; official CCC 2016 record verified.
sources.assessment: The hierarchy is against a bounded sublinear advice exponent. The circuit application is NP-uniform and fixed-size-degree. RE uses one-sided exponential randomness; its lower bound does not give NE/NEXP versus BPP. No NPpoly or Ppoly exclusion follows by dropping qualifiers.

sources.title: Nonrelativizing Separations
sources.locator: CCC 1998 pp.8–12; Section 3 definition of MAEXP; Theorem 3.4 and Corollaries 3.5–3.6, printed p.10; Section 4
sources.read_depth: Read the final published five-page primary PDF, including the exponential verifier definition and the nonrelativizing separation argument.
sources.assessment: MAEXP⊄Ppoly and PEXP⊄Ppoly do not give NEXP⊄Ppoly or EXP⊄Ppoly. PEXP here is exponential-time majority, and MAEXP retains probabilistic verification and exponential messages. Its relativized circuit inclusion is an oracle result.

sources.title: Robust Simulations and Significant Separations
sources.locator: Theorems 28 and 30; Proposition 36; introductory theorem scope
sources.read_depth: Read the author journal manuscript theorem statements, including explicit Promise-MAEXP in Theorem 30; publication chain includes 2010 preprint, ICALP 2011 and TAMC 2015.
sources.version_limitation: The arXiv original and later journal manuscript are not treated as identical versions. No new baseline theorem is imported from the current PDF.
sources.assessment: Robustly-often circuit results retain a fixed size degree or an explicit promise class. NEXP versus ACC0 and nondeterministic/co-nondeterministic hierarchy consequences already have baseline labels. Strengthening the frequency of a separation does not by itself add a roster pair.

sources.title: Constructive Separations and Their Consequences
sources.read_depth: Rechecked the theorem premise and parameterized class list; this source was already reviewed in earlier rounds, so it is corroboration rather than newly discovered independent evidence.
sources.assessment: The constructive conclusion assumes a separation; membership of a class in its parameter list does not assert that every listed pair is known separated or known open. The abstract specifically treats ZPP versus EXP and BPP versus NEXP as major open examples.

basic_sanity_checks.deduction: Any noninclusion with both endpoints in this block would imply P≠NP. This is a consequence of the cited baseline, not a proof that no missing known inclusion exists.

conditional_recheck.derivation: Assume RP⊆P and EXP⊆BPP. NP⊆EXP gives NP⊆BPP, so the baseline self-reduction implication gives NP⊆RP⊆P. PH collapses to P; BPP⊆PH then gives EXP⊆P, contradicting the deterministic time hierarchy.
conditional_recheck.status: Logical scope check only; no unconditional pair and no new rule imported.

reviewed: Finite fair-coin sample space and all-input halting/error conditions.
MA witness chosen before randomness versus AM witness depending on the public random string.
Finite coefficient lists specify witness/random lengths; polynomial verifier runs on an injective tuple encoding.
NPpoly advice depends only on input length and is intentionally arbitrary subject to its polynomial bound.
Theta2P bounds adaptive oracle queries by a constant times log2(n+1)+1; Delta2P does not inherit a fixed global polynomial query exponent.
limitations: Not a new complete proof of model equivalence.
Not a complete rereview of low-level tape and transducer implementation.

incremental_basic_model_application.basis: Concrete finite randomness and verifier/oracle definitions plus selected quantifier-order and budget checks reduce obvious mismatches; textbook equivalence proofs are incomplete, so a shared interpretation error with many basic-pair consequences remains possible.
